stance_basis: research cited as informational reference on highway salt contamination risk, no position taken on the project
summary: James M. Weigle of the U.S. Geological Survey is cited as the author of a report titled 'Ground-water Contamination by Highway Salting,' which is referenced in the EIS to assess the potential impact of road salt on shallow dolomite aquifer wells serving Chicago Heights, Park Forest, Matteson, and Olympia Fields. Excerpts from his report describe how salt applied to highways can migrate into groundwater, with chloride concentrations varying by location. His research is used by the document preparers to contextualize the water quality discussion, not to express a position on the project itself.
complaint_summary: Weigle's USGS report on groundwater contamination by highway salting is cited to discuss the possibility that road salt application could affect shallow dolomite aquifer wells supplying municipal water to communities along the Lincoln Highway corridor.
summary_quote: The possibility of these types of wells being effected by application of salt to highway surfaces has been discussed by James M. Weigle of the U.S. Geological Survey in the report entitled "Ground-water Contamination by Highway Salting."
